title: React Working Flow: From Components to UI
description: Understand how React works from start to finish — components, JSX, props, state, events, rendering, the Virtual DOM, re-renders, hooks, and how React updates the browser UI.

title: Object Oriented Programming
description: Master OOP for LLD: classes, objects, responsibilities, encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces, abstract classes, and object relationships such as association, aggregation, composition, and dependency. Build strong object-thinking skills and choose composition vs inheritance effectively.

title: DSA Pattern Recognition Cheat Sheet
description: A quick-reference guide covering 25 recurring DSA patterns, their trigger clues, and recognition techniques to help you identify the right pattern before writing code.

title: Computer Networks Part 1: From Bits to NAT
description: Build a strong mental model of networking from layers, bits, signals, and NICs to frames, MAC addresses, switches, IP addressing, routers, ARP, IPv4, private/public IPs, and NAT.

title: Computer Networks Part 2: Transport Layer, Ports & Sockets
description: Understand how networking moves from host-to-host delivery to application-level communication through ports, TCP and UDP, ephemeral ports, 4-tuples, sockets, listening connections, and NAT port mapping.

title: Computer Networks Part 3: TCP Reliability & Congestion Control
description: Dive into TCP internals including the 3-way handshake, sequence numbers, ACKs, retransmission, out-of-order data, sliding windows, flow control, congestion control, Slow Start, connection termination, FIN, RST, and TIME_WAIT.

title: Computer Networks Part 4: DNS, HTTP, HTTPS & CDN
description: Understand how applications communicate over the network through DNS resolution, HTTP requests and responses, HTTPS with TLS and certificates, HTTP caching, and CDNs that deliver content closer to users.

title: Computer Networks Part 5: Proxies, Architecture & Network Security
description: Complete the SDE-1 networking picture with CDNs, forward and reverse proxies, load balancers, VPNs, API gateways, 3-tier architecture, monoliths vs microservices, CORS, network security, common attacks, MTU, PMTUD, and end-to-end request flows.

title: System Design Fundamentals & Networking
description: Learn core system design concepts including scalability, availability, reliability, performance, fault tolerance, and trade-offs. Understand DNS, TCP/UDP, HTTP/HTTPS, TLS, REST, authentication, sessions, JWT, load balancers, and databases. Practice client-server architecture, request flows, bottleneck identification, and scaling real-world systems.

title: System Design - 2 (OOPS)
description: Master OOP for LLD: classes, objects, responsibilities, encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces, abstract classes, and object relationships such as association, aggregation, composition, and dependency. Build strong object-thinking skills and choose composition vs inheritance effectively.

title: System Design - 3 - Design Concepts and Parking Lot (Example)
description: Master OOP for LLD: classes, objects, responsibilities, encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces, abstract classes, and object relationships such as association, aggregation, composition, and dependency. Build strong object-thinking skills and choose composition vs inheritance effectively.

title: System Design - 4 - Scalability, Load Balancing & Database Design
description: Master system scalability and database design: scaling, load balancing, bottlenecks, failover, SQL vs NoSQL, indexes, transactions, ACID, replication, partitioning, sharding, caching, and read/write splitting. Practice designing systems for 100× traffic and 10M+ users.

title: System Design - 5 - Caching, Async Systems & Queues
description: Master caching and asynchronous system design: cache hits and misses, invalidation, TTL, cache stampede, request coalescing, timeouts, backpressure, fail-fast, queues, workers, acknowledgements, retries, idempotency, transactional outbox, dead letter queues, worker scaling, and system monitoring.

title: Machine Learning Part 1: Types of Machine Learning
description: Understand supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised and reinforcement learning, including regression, classification, clustering, dimensionality reduction and anomaly detection.

title: Feature Engineering Part 1: Fundamentals, Scaling, Encoding & Pipelines
description: Learn the machine learning lifecycle, feature preprocessing, standardization, normalization, categorical encoding, fit vs transform, ColumnTransformer and Scikit-learn pipelines.

title: Feature Engineering Part 2: Transformations & Special Variables
description: Explore FunctionTransformer, PowerTransformer, Box-Cox and Yeo-Johnson transformations, binning, binarization, mixed variables and date-time feature extraction using practical Python examples.

title: Feature Engineering Part 3: Missing Data & Imputation
description: Learn complete case analysis, mean, median and mode imputation, arbitrary values, random sample imputation, missing indicators, KNN imputation and MICE (Iterative Imputer).

title: Feature Engineering Part 4: Outlier Detection & Treatment
description: Understand outliers, their impact on machine learning models, Z-score, IQR and percentile detection methods, along with trimming, capping and winsorization using practical Python code.

title: Gradient Descent: Batch, Stochastic & Mini-Batch
description: Learn how Gradient Descent optimizes model parameters using loss functions, gradients and learning rates. Compare Batch, Stochastic (SGD) and Mini-Batch Gradient Descent with mathematical intuition and practical Python implementations.

title: Linear Regression: Simple & Multiple Linear Regression
description: Understand simple and multiple linear regression, slope, intercept, least squares, normal equations, coefficient interpretation, multicollinearity and regression evaluation metrics such as MAE, MSE, RMSE, R² and Adjusted R².

title: Polynomial Regression & Bias-Variance Trade-off
description: Learn how polynomial features capture nonlinear patterns, how to choose the degree, and how bias, variance and noise explain underfitting and overfitting, with practical Python code.

title: Regularization: Ridge, Lasso & ElasticNet
description: Learn how Ridge (L2), Lasso (L1) and ElasticNet regularization penalize large coefficients to control overfitting, how alpha and l1_ratio work, and how to select them using cross-validation with practical Python code.
